name: Renaissance Global Ltd
title: Renaissance Global Ltd - 532923 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Renaissance Global Q1 FY27 revenue rose 30% YoY to INR690 crores and PAT jumped 288% to INR26 crores, but management guided revenue down as low-return customers are exited.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 30% YoY to INR690 crores (ex-bullion) and EBITDA rose 22% to INR50 crores, with PAT up sharply to about INR26 crores helped by a weak prior-year restructuring charge. Owned-brand revenue grew 29% to INR89 crores and owned-brand EBITDA margin improved to 11.5% from 10%. Working capital days fell to 220 from 253 YoY. Management said it will exit low-return customer businesses in the customer brands segment, which lowers revenue run-rate by INR400 crores by year-end, while it targets bottom-line growth above 30% for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: from 7.7% a year ago (management's comparison, ex-bullion)

segments.name: Owned brands (D2C)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR89 crores, up 29% YoY; EBITDA margin 11.5% vs 10%. Focus on Jean Dousset and WithClarity, which together make up the bulk of owned-brand revenue. WithClarity run-rate about INR220 crores, growing about 20%.

segments.name: Licensed brands
segments.commentary: Management is rationalising licences (exiting NFL, Netflix, Harry Potter and others) to focus on Disney, where it is exclusive licensee for fine jewellery. Management said licensed-brand margin fell from 15.5% in FY24 to 10.9% in Q1 FY27 and expects a return to 14-15%.

segments.name: Customer brands (B2B/OEM)
segments.commentary: Where the planned exits sit. Management expects INR300-400 crores of annualised revenue to be removed, with the revenue run-rate down INR400 crores by year-end. Sequential revenue declines expected from Q2.

guidance_outlook: Bottom line expected to grow more than 30% in FY27, with revenue growth muted by customer exits.
Working capital release of about INR250 crores and operating cash flow above INR300 crores in FY27, to be realised by year-end.

Target of INR1,000 crores direct-to-consumer revenue by FY29 with at least 15% operating margin on that segment; FY27 D2C base is about INR500 crores (INR375 crores owned brands, INR125 crores licensed).
Jean Dousset: 7 stores by end FY27 (3 operating today, 4 more planned), then 6 more in FY28; management says each store should add INR25-35 crores of sales and pay back in under 1 year.
Management expects a minor margin dip during the year from exit costs, with margins comparable like-for-like.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity was reduced to match lab-grown diamond realities, with 24 months of restructuring cutting operating expenses by about INR45 crores annually.
Jean Dousset: company owns 65% after exercising an option up from 38.7%; a further stake increase is possible only if more funding is needed and has not yet been discussed at board level.
Tariff mitigation: some manufacturing subcontracted in the US and Middle East, which generates bullion sales.
Possible tariff refunds under application; amount not yet quantified and customers may share in refunds.
demand_pricing: Customer brands exits: management said the exited customers are low-return, with working capital costs above EBITDA generated; inventory exit cost is negligible because gold and silver prices have risen.
Average order values by tier: licensed brands about USD400, WithClarity about USD3,000, Jean Dousset about USD8,000. Customer brands range from USD50 to USD3,000.
Jean Dousset and WithClarity gross margins are 60-65%; WithClarity EBITDA margin is 11-13%.
Forex loss of about INR13 crores in Q1 (rupee appreciation); a large share of working capital is dollar-denominated, giving a natural hedge.
Metal price exposure hedged, with no inventory loss reported in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth continue at Q1's pace, and what about US tariff refunds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects bottom-line momentum to continue but revenue growth may not hold as low-return verticals are exited. Tariff refunds are being applied for; the amount was not disclosed and management asked investors to wait one more quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Which segment will the INR250 crore working-capital release come from, and how big is the revenue hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Release comes from inventory and receivables, mainly in customer brands. Exits remove INR300-400 crores of annualised revenue, and the revenue run-rate falls INR400 crores by year-end; the company expects no meaningful bottom-line impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why are licensed-brand revenue and margins declining?
qa_highlights.answer: Management rationalised a wide licence portfolio, exiting NFL, Netflix, Harry Potter and others, with exit costs taken. It expects growth and margin recovery to 14-15% from focusing on Disney.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Jean Dousset's revenue is reported, and what is store economics?
qa_highlights.answer: The company consolidates Jean Dousset in full with a 65% stake, and minority interest is shown in the P&L. Brand revenue grew about 30% after acquisition in FY26; each store should add INR25-35 crores of sales and pay back in under 1 year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin decline and will B2B revenue keep rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Bullion sales are a continuing feature because of tariff-mitigation subcontracting. Ex-bullion margin fell from 7.7% to 7.2% due to exit costs. Sequential revenue should decline from Q2, tapering through Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 finance cost trajectory and forex loss outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give quarterly finance cost guidance but expects meaningfully lower net debt YoY by year-end. The forex loss should ease if the currency stabilises at current levels; other income of INR8-9 crores was described as normal course.

risks_watch: Revenue run-rate falls by INR400 crores by year-end from customer exits; revenue growth may turn negative sequentially from Q2.
Achieving INR250 crores working-capital release and INR300 crores operating cash flow in FY27.
Quality of PAT: the 288% jump is partly base effect from prior-year restructuring costs; Q1 forex loss of about INR13 crores.
Jean Dousset store ramp: 4 new stores in FY27 and 6 in FY28 need funding; a further stake increase or third-party investor is not yet discussed.
Tariff refund amount and how much will be passed to customers remain unquantified.
Licensed-brand margin recovery (10.9% to 14-15%) and rising Disney revenue are not yet shown in numbers.
